36874-a-girl-in-spring-time.title: A Girl In Spring Time
36874-a-girl-in-spring-time.creator: Jessie Mansergh
36874-a-girl-in-spring-time.description: A book by Jessie Mansergh. pattern, and held herself with a like air of dignified composure. Bertha and Lois Faucit were the daughters of a dean who lived in an old cathedral town, and their school-fellows were accustomed to account for every peculiarity on this score. "Dean's daughters, you know!"  It was ridiculous to expect that the children of such a dignitary would indulge in pillow-fights, and bedroom supper, like ordinary frivolous mortals.

arxiv-2102-05630.title: VOICE CLONING: A MULTI-SPEAKER TEXT-TO-SPEECH SYNTHESIS APPROACH BASED ON TRANSFER LEARNING
arxiv-2102-05630.creator: Giuseppe Ruggiero, Enrico Zovato, Luigi Di Caro, Vincent Pollet
arxiv-2102-05630.description: Abstract Deep learning models are becoming predominant in many fields of machine learning. Text-to-Speech (TTS), the process of synthesizing artificial speech from text, is no exception. To this end, a deep neural network is usually trained using a corpus of several hours of recorded speech from a single speaker.

arxiv-2107-10062.title: Projection methods for high numerical aperture phase retrieval
arxiv-2107-10062.creator: Nguyen Hieu Thao, Oleg Soloviev, Russell Luke, Michel Verhaegen
arxiv-2107-10062.description: Abstract We develop for the first time a mathematical framework in which the class of projection algorithms can be applied to high numerical aperture (NA) phase retrieval. Within this framework, we first analyze the basic steps of solving the high-NA phase retrieval problem by projection algorithms and establish the closed forms of all the relevant prox-operators.

arxiv-2205-03319.title: Wave-driven outbursts and variability of low-mass supernova progenitors
arxiv-2205-03319.creator: Samantha C. Wu, Jim Fuller
arxiv-2205-03319.description: Abstract In a substantial number of core-collapse supernovae, early-time interaction indicates a dense circumstellar medium (CSM) that may be produced by outbursts from the progenitor star. Wave-driven mass loss is a possible mechanism to produce these signatures, with previous work suggesting this mechanism is most effective for low mass ( ∼ 11 ​ M ⊙ \sim\!11\,M_{\odot} ) SN progenitors.

arxiv-2212-07593.title: Enhanced Training of Query-Based Object Detection via Selective Query Recollection
arxiv-2212-07593.creator: Fangyi Chen, Han Zhang, Kai Hu, Yu-Kai Huang, Chenchen Zhu, Marios Savvides, Carnegie Mellon University, Meta AI {fangyic,hanz3,kaihu,yukaih2,marioss}@andrew.cmu.edu chenchenz@fb.com
arxiv-2212-07593.description: Abstract This paper investigates a phenomenon where query-based object detectors mispredict at the last decoding stage while predicting correctly at an intermediate stage. We review the training process and attribute the overlooked phenomenon to two limitations: lack of training emphasis and cascading errors from decoding sequence.

arxiv-2505-23286.title: Eulers Horizonte – Möglichkeiten und Grenzen seiner Arbeitsweise in der Mathematik
arxiv-2505-23286.creator: Alexander Aycock
arxiv-2505-23286.description: Abstract 1 Geleitwort Lest EULER - er ist unser aller Meister! Pierre–Simon Laplace Leonhard Euler (1707–1783) war unumstritten einer der produktivsten und vielseitigsten Mathematiker aller Zeiten. Seine gesammelten Werke umfassen mittlerweile 4 Reihen bestehend aus insgesamt 84 Büchern von je 300 bis 700 Seiten, sodass sich sein Opus in Gänze auf ungefähr 30000 beläuft.

arxiv-2508-07678.title: Abundance and phase-space distribution of subhalos in cosmological N-body simulations: testing numerical convergence and correction methods
arxiv-2508-07678.creator: Kun Xu
arxiv-2508-07678.description: Abstract Subhalos play a crucial role in accurately modeling galaxy formation and galaxy-based cosmological probes within the highly nonlinear, virialized regime. However, numerical convergence of subhalo evolution is difficult to achieve, especially in the inner regions of host halos where tidal forces are strongest.

pmc-11645832.title: P034 Noxturnal cRIP: An alternative to AASM recommended flow sensors in analysis of respiratory events in polysomnography
pmc-11645832.creator: N Eriksson, L Burr
pmc-11645832.description: IntroductionAASM recommends the use of nasal pressure (NP), oronasal thermal flow (Th), and respiratory inductance plethysmography (RIP) for detecting and characterising respiratory events (RE) in polysomnography. A previous comparative study assessed utility of Noxturnal RIP flow (cRIPflow) as an alternative to Th for identification of RE in polysomnography.

pmc-12952548.title: Artificial Intelligence–enabled Automatic Computed Tomography Segmentation for Craniomaxillofacial Surgery Using a Real Surgical Database
pmc-12952548.creator: Songying Wu, Pui Hang Leung, Andy Wai Kan Yeung, May Chun Mei Wong, Kar Yan Li, Taku Komura, Wei-fa Yang, Yu-xiong Su
pmc-12952548.description: Background:Skull computed tomography (CT) segmentation is the cornerstone of computer-assisted craniomaxillofacial surgery. Clinical routine threshold-based segmentation is time-consuming and yields suboptimal results in critical anatomical regions. This study evaluated the performance of an artificial intelligence (AI)–enabled automatic segmentation of skull CT scans and investigated clinical factors affecting its performance.

pmc-13040394.title: Driving Distance From US Jails to Opioid Treatment Programs
pmc-13040394.creator: Brendan Saloner, Allison O’Rourke, Kristianny Ruelas-Vargas, Minna Song, Kelly S. Ramsey, Sachini Bandara
pmc-13040394.description: This cross-sectional study quantifies access to methadone for incarcerated people in the US in terms of distance between jails and opioid treatment programs. Introduction Providing medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD) in carceral facilities is associated with markedly decreased postrelease overdose risk.1 Starting MOUD during incarceration is challenging particularly in jails, where lengths of stay are short and often unpredictable.
